intro: Content planners on Mac use Notion as a central hub to manage calendars, briefs, and assets. You can organize your entire editorial pipeline in one place, but the manual work of updating databases and switching between apps often slows you down. By pairing Notion with Lazur, you can automate your voice commands and navigation to keep your focus on the strategy instead of the interface.
tldr: Use Notion databases to track content status and deadlines.
Master keyboard shortcuts like ⌘ + P to search your workspace quickly.
Set up a custom content calendar template to save time on recurring projects.
Use Lazur to dictate notes, set reminders, and navigate your Mac while you work in Notion.
Keep your workspace clean by archiving old pages to the Trash regularly.

blocks.text: Why content planners choose Notion on Mac

Notion works well on macOS because it allows for high customization. You can build a system that matches your specific content cycle. Whether you are tracking blog posts, social media updates, or video scripts, you need a single source of truth. Many planners find that the desktop app is more stable than the browser version for long sessions.

Start by creating a database. Press / and type database to see your options. Use a Board view to see your content stages like Draft, Review, and Published. You can drag cards between columns to update status. This visual approach helps you see bottlenecks before they become late projects.
Essential Notion shortcuts for Mac users

items: ⌘ + P: Open the search bar to find any page.
⌘ + N: Create a new page in your current location.
⌘ + ⇧ + L: Toggle dark mode to reduce eye strain.
Shift + ?: Open the full list of keyboard shortcuts.
/: Open the block menu to add images, tables, or toggles.

blocks.text: How to stay focused with Lazur

Interruptions break your flow. Research shows it takes over 23 minutes to get back on track after a distraction. When you use Lazur, you can ask questions without leaving your Notion window. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask about a date on your calendar. Lazur answers out loud, so you do not have to alt tab to your calendar app.

Avoid clutter by using templates. If you write the same type of brief every week, create a template inside your database. Go to the arrow next to the New button in your database. Click + New template. Fill it out once. Now, every time you add a new row, the content is ready for you.
Use the Notion desktop app to ensure you can use system-wide shortcuts. If you ever see an error, check the Notion menu in the top bar to see if an update is available.
blocks.title: Keep the app updated

items: Overcomplicating your database properties: Keep it simple so you actually use it.
Forgetting to archive: If a project is done, move it to an archive page.
Ignoring permissions: If you work with a team, check your sharing settings early.
Not using search: Stop scrolling through your sidebar. Use ⌘ + P instead.

blocks.text: Link your content calendar to a task list. Use a Relation property to connect your content database to a separate task database. This allows you to see exactly which subtasks are holding up a publication date. If you need to research a topic, use the Lazur for Chrome extension. It runs the research in the background and gives you a report so you can paste the findings directly into your Notion page.

Your content is private. Lazur only sees your screen when you hold the shortcut key. It does not store your audio or screenshots. This is important when you are working on sensitive client briefs or upcoming product launches.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my Notion pages directly?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or edit files. It helps you by answering questions, dictating text, and guiding your actions.

faq.question: What is the best way to start with Notion?
faq.answer: Start with a simple page for your notes. Once you feel comfortable, create a database for your content calendar.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on older Mac models?
faq.answer: Lazur supports macOS on both Apple silicon and Intel chips. Ensure you are on a supported version of macOS.
